This is the **spring-petclinic-rest** project (Spring Boot, Maven). There is currently **no `customerCode` field anywhere** in the main source — it only exists in the acceptance test that specifies the feature. ### 1. Owner entity/model
- **`/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/model/Owner.java`**
  - `@Entity @Table(name = "owners")`, extends `Person`.
  - Own fields: `address`, `city`, `telephone` (E.164 `^\+[0-9]{8,15}$`), `email`, `registrationDate` (LocalDate), `pets` (OneToMany). No `customerCode` yet.
- **`lastName` lives in the parent** `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/model/Person.java` (`@MappedSuperclass`):
  - `protected String firstName;` (`@Column(name="first_name")`), `protected String lastName;` (`@Column(name="last_name")`), both `@NotEmpty`, with getters/setters.
  - Base id/isNew logic is in `BaseEntity` (same `model` package).
- To persist a `customerCode`, add a `@Column(name = "customer_code")` field + getter/setter here, and add the column to the H2 schema (`src/main/resources/db/h2/schema.sql` — worth confirming).

### 2. Service that creates/saves owners
- Interface: **`/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/service/ClinicService.java`** — `void saveOwner(Owner owner)` (line 59).
- Impl: **`/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/service/ClinicServiceImpl.java`** (lines 232-237):
  ```java
  @Override @Transactional
  public void saveOwner(Owner owner) throws DataAccessException {
      ownerRepository.save(owner);
  }
  ```
  Injects `OwnerRepository ownerRepository` (line 45). This is the natural place to compute/assign `customerCode` before `save`, if you want it applied regardless of controller.

### 3. Owner repository
- Interface: **`/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/repository/OwnerRepository.java`** — methods: `findByLastName(String)`, `findByLastName(String, Pageable)`, `findById(int)`, `save(Owner)`, `findAll()`, `findAll(Pageable)`, `delete(Owner)`.
  - **There is NO `count()` method** on this interface. For a global sequence you must add one.
- Active implementation (profile `spring-data-jpa`): **`/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/repository/springdatajpa/SpringDataOwnerRepository.java`** — a Spring Data `Repository<Owner, Integer>`. Since it extends Spring Data `Repository`, you can declare a derived `long count()` (or a `@Query("SELECT COUNT(owner) FROM Owner owner")`) and Spring Data will implement it. It already uses `SELECT COUNT(owner) FROM Owner owner` count queries for pagination (lines 46, 52).
- Other (inactive-by-default) impls that also would need a matching `count()` if you add it to the interface:

  - `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/repository/jdbc/JdbcOwnerRepositoryImpl.java` (`save()` at line 152).

    ProblemDetail:
      title: Problem Detail
      description: The schema for all error responses.
      type: object
      properties:
        type:
          title: Type

          minimum: 400
          maximum: 600

          title: Detail

      required:

      title: Validation message

          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: >-
            The telephone number of the pet owner. On create it is normalized to
            E.164 form: a leading '+' and country code are kept when present,
            otherwise the country code '+61' is assumed and a single leading '0' is
            dropped from the national digits; spaces, dashes and brackets are
            stripped. The result must carry 8 to 15 digits after the '+'. The stored
            and returned value is this E.164 string, e.g. '0412 345 678' becomes
            '+61412345678'.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          example: '+61412345678'
        email:
          title: Email address
          description: >-
            The email address of the pet owner. Optional; when present it must be a
            syntactically valid address. The stored and returned value is lower-cased.
          type: string
          format: email
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: 'george.franklin@example.com'
        registrationDate:
          title: Registration date
          description: >-

            Optional on create; when omitted it defaults to the server's current
            date.

          format: date

## Summary

I implemented the `customerCode` feature so owners are assigned a code formatted `<LAST3>-<NNNN>` on creation.

**What each part does:**
- **`model/Owner.java`** — added a `customerCode` field (`@Column(name = "customer_code")`) with getter/setter so the value is persisted and read back on `GET /api/owners/{id}`.
- **`rest/controller/v1/OwnerRestControllerV1.java`** — in the create path (`addOwner`), assigns the code via a new `nextCustomerCode(lastName)` helper before saving:
  - `LAST3` = first three letters of `lastName`, upper-cased (guarded with `Math.min(3, length)` for short names).
  - `NNNN` = `findAllOwners().size() + 1`, zero-padded to 4 digits — a **global** sequence equal to one more than the current owner count. Because the first owner is persisted (and auto-flushed) before the second's count query runs, the second code is exactly the first + 1, satisfying the test's `SMI-` / `JON-` global-sequence assertion.
- **`resources/openapi.yml`** — added a read-only `customerCode` property to the `Owner` schema, so the generated `OwnerDto` exposes it and MapStruct auto-maps the same-named entity property through to the response (no mapper change needed).
- **Schema files** — added the `customer_code` column to all four DB schemas (`h2`, `hsqldb`, `mysql`, `postgres`); the tests run on `hsqldb`, which was the source of the initial `InvalidDataAccessResourceUsageException` before I added the column there. The column is nullable so existing seed inserts remain valid.

**Test result:** `./mvnw test` → `Tests run: 1, Failures: 0, Errors: 0` — BUILD SUCCESS.
